claims.claim_text: Strong High = manipulated up + broke structure DOWN (BOS) + returns to it (RTO zone) = great short. Strong Low = manipulated down + broke structure UP (BOS) + returns = great long. Weak High = from a strong low, broke nothing = liquidity target. Weak Low = from a strong high, failed to break = will be broken later.
Major structure (swing LH/LL) vs Internal structure (fractal sub-waves within it); if major structure is bearish, short when price moves higher; understanding both improves timing.

claims.claim_text: A structure break (BOS) happens when a key swing point is broken -> shift bearish<->bullish. Displacement = a strong, fast price move that breaks key levels with high momentum (Candle close). Wait for confirmation to avoid fakeouts.

claims.claim_text: A valid Single Candle Order Block (SCOB): candle close above the inducement zone / candle close below = Point of Interest (POI). Confluences (volume analysis; daily/weekly/monthly session levels) strengthen it; 'the more confluences align, the stronger the trade setup'.

claims.claim_text: Three types of price inefficiency: Volume imbalance, Fair value gap, Opening gap. Price tends to return to fill them, providing entry areas; opening-gap reversal back to the gap = a good entry.
claims.provenance_note: caption 'Types of price inefficiencies' + 3 named types; END of post

claims.claim_text: Trend Continuation entry: a Low-Time-Frame Break of Structure (BOS) leaves an FVG; price fills the gap (mitigation) and continues. Be patient (setups take time); manage risk (size to loss, set targets).

High-Probability POI entry: strong move breaks a prior pattern -> POI/imbalance origin -> liquidity develops both sides -> gradual return toward origin -> sweep into the POI -> lower-timeframe confirmation -> target opposing liquidity. Checklist: confirmation on a smaller TF; areas with lots of liquidity; patience.
